newsitem.title: FINLAND: HARTWALL SAYS BBH TO INVEST IN RUSSIA.
newsitem.headline: HARTWALL SAYS BBH TO INVEST IN RUSSIA.

text.p: Finnish beverages group Oy Hartwall Ab said on Wednesday its half-owned Baltic Beverages Holding (BBH) unit planned a joint venture with French Groupe Soufflet to build a malting plant in Russia for $50 million.
Groupe Soufflet would own 70 percent and BBH's Baltika brewery would own 30 percent of the joint venture, Hartwall said in a statement.
Norwegian Orkla's Pripps-Ringnes owns the other half of BBH.
"The investment will be divided into two stages, each of which is valued at about $25 million," Hartwall said, adding the unit would be built in St Petersburg.
The new plant would be completed in 1999 and with an initial capacity of 75,000 tonnes of malt per year, later rising to 150,000 tonnes, and it would create about new 50 jobs, it said.
"It will produce 40 percent of the malt that is consumed in Russia," it said.
BBH's Baltika brewery, founded in 1990, is the largest in Russia and it is expected to produce about 250 million litres of beer this year, Hartwall said.
Baltic Beverages Holding AB operates seven breweries, three in the Baltic countries, three in Russia and one in Ukraine, Hartwall said.
